subproblems.title: Continuity of the inverse of a Simon local representation on W ∩ M (Simon 2.4.2)
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, r ∈ ℕ∞, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ satisfy IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ: V and W are open, ψ is C^r on V, ψ is injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(x) is injective for every x ∈ V. Let g := Function.invFunOn ψ V : ℝᴺ → ℝⁿ. Here g(y) is a point of V mapped to y by ψ whenever such a point exists, and a fixed arbitrary point of ℝⁿ otherwise. Then g is continuous on W ∩ M in the relative topology, that is, ContinuousOn g (W ∩ M).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ → ContinuousOn (Function.invFunOn ψ V) (W ∩ M)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof of simon_submanifold_tangent_basics, written out for the inverse map g = Function.invFunOn ψ V. This is Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, 4.2, p. 55, where the printed text only says that the definition ensures the local representation is a homeomorphism of V onto M ∩ W.

Hypotheses used: V and W are open; ψ is C^r on V for some r ∈ ℕ∞; ψ is injective on V; ψ(V) = W ∩ M; and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact for every compact Q ⊆ W. Injectivity of Dψ is not needed.

Proof.
1. ψ is continuous on V. A C^r map on V (any r ≥ 0) is continuous on V. Since V is open, ψ is continuous at every point of V.
2. g inverts ψ on W ∩ M. Let y ∈ W ∩ M. Since ψ(V) = W ∩ M, some a ∈ V has ψ(a) = y, so by the definition of invFunOn, g(y) ∈ V and ψ(g(y)) = y. Since ψ is injective on V, g(y) is the unique point of V mapped to y. In particular g(ψ(x)) = x for every x ∈ V.
3. Reduction to sequences. ℝⁿ and ℝᴺ are metric spaces, hence first countable. So g is continuous within W ∩ M at a point y ∈ W ∩ M as soon as g(y_j) → g(y) for every sequence (y_j) in W ∩ M with y_j → y. Fix y ∈ W ∩ M and such a sequence, and put x_j := g(y_j) and x := g(y). By step 2, x_j, x ∈ V, ψ(x_j) = y_j and ψ(x) = y.
4. A compact set containing all x_j. Q := {y_j : j ∈ ℕ} ∪ {y} is compact, being a convergent sequence together with its limit. Q ⊆ W, because every y_j and y lie in W ∩ M. By relative properness, K := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact. Each x_j lies in V with ψ(x_j) = y_j ∈ Q, so x_j ∈ K.
5. Subsequential limits. Let (x_{j_k}) be any subsequence. K is a compact subset of the metric space ℝⁿ, hence sequentially compact, so some further subsequence (x_{j_{k_l}}) converges to a point x′ ∈ K ⊆ V. By step 1, ψ is continuous at x′, so ψ(x_{j_{k_l}}) → ψ(x′). But ψ(x_{j_{k_l}}) = y_{j_{k_l}} → y. By uniqueness of limits ψ(x′) = y = ψ(x), and injectivity of ψ on V gives x′ = x.
6. Convergence. Suppose x_j does not converge to x. Then there are ε > 0 and a subsequence with |x_{j_k} − x| ≥ ε for all k. By step 5 this subsequence has a further subsequence converging to x, a contradiction. Hence g(y_j) = x_j → x = g(y).
7. Conclusion. By steps 3 and 6, g is continuous within W ∩ M at every point of W ∩ M, that is, ContinuousOn (Function.invFunOn ψ V) (W ∩ M).

Formal references:
- SimonGMT Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation.isProperMap_chartMap and isEmbedding_chartMap (Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter02/SubmanifoldTopology.lean) prove the equivalent statement that the corestriction V → W of ψ is a closed topological embedding.
- Mathlib: Function.invFunOn_mem, Function.invFunOn_eq, Set.InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn, Filter.Tendsto.isCompact_insert_range, IsCompact.tendsto_subseq.
proof_key_steps: ψ is continuous at every point of the open set V (C^r implies C⁰). g = invFunOn ψ V returns the unique ψ-preimage in V of every y ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V).
Reduce continuity on W ∩ M to sequences y_j → y in W ∩ M, since metric spaces are first countable.
Q = {y_j} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so relative properness makes V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) a compact set containing every x_j = g(y_j).
Every subsequence of (x_j) has a further subsequence converging to some x′ ∈ V with ψ(x′) = y, so x′ = g(y) by injectivity. The sub-subsequence criterion then gives g(y_j) → g(y).

subproblems.title: Tangent space of a Simon submanifold equals the range of the chart derivative (Simon 2.4.3)
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, r ∈ ℕ∞ with 1 ≤ r, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ satisfy IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ: V and W are open, ψ is C^r on V, ψ is injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(x) is injective for x ∈ V. Then for every x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x), where Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x. Here tangentSpace M y is the linear span of all vectors γ′(0) such that γ : ℝ → ℝᴺ is C¹ on (−1,1), maps (−1,1) into M, satisfies γ(0) = y and has derivative γ′(0) at 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)) (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), 1 ≤ r → Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ → ∀ x ∈ V, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x).toLinearMap
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–4 of the parent-supplied proof of simon_submanifold_tangent_basics. This is Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, 4.3, p. 55: T_yM is a linear subspace with basis D₁ψ(x), …, D_nψ(x); the printed text only says 'one readily checks'. Step 1 of the parent proof (continuity of ψ⁻¹ on W ∩ M) is the sibling theorem chart_inverse_continuous, used in step 7 below.

Setting and notation. Fix x₀ ∈ V. Put y₀ := ψ(x₀), A := Dψ(x₀) = fderiv ℝ ψ x₀, and T := range A, a linear subspace of ℝᴺ. Let G be the set of generators of tangentSpace M y₀: v ∈ G iff there is γ : ℝ → ℝᴺ that is C¹ on (−1,1), maps (−1,1) into M, has γ(0) = y₀ and has derivative v at 0. Thus tangentSpace M y₀ = span G. Note that y₀ ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M.

Proof.
1. Differentiability. V is open and ψ is C^r on V with r ≥ 1, so ψ is C¹ on V and differentiable at every point x of V, with derivative fderiv ℝ ψ x. Write e(x) := ψ(x) − ψ(x₀) − A(x − x₀). Then for every ε > 0 there is δ_ε > 0 with |e(x)| ≤ ε|x − x₀| whenever |x − x₀| < δ_ε.

Part A: T ⊆ tangentSpace M y₀.
2. Let w ∈ ℝⁿ. If w = 0, then Aw = 0 ∈ tangentSpace M y₀. Now let w ≠ 0. Choose ρ > 0 with B(x₀, ρ) ⊆ V, which is possible because V is open. Put c := ρ/(2|w|) > 0, ℓ(t) := x₀ + c t w and γ(t) := ψ(ℓ(t)) for t ∈ ℝ.
3. For t ∈ (−1,1), |ℓ(t) − x₀| = c|t||w| < ρ/2, so ℓ(t) ∈ V and γ(t) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M ⊆ M. The affine map ℓ is C^∞ and maps (−1,1) into V, and ψ is C¹ on V, so γ = ψ ∘ ℓ is C¹ on (−1,1). Also γ(0) = ψ(x₀) = y₀.
4. We have ℓ(0) = x₀ and ℓ′(0) = c w, and ψ is differentiable at x₀ with derivative A. The chain rule gives γ′(0) = A(c w) = c·Aw. Hence c·Aw ∈ G ⊆ tangentSpace M y₀. Since tangentSpace M y₀ is a linear subspace, Aw = c⁻¹·(c·Aw) ∈ tangentSpace M y₀. Thus T ⊆ tangentSpace M y₀.

Part B: tangentSpace M y₀ ⊆ T.
5. T is a linear subspace and tangentSpace M y₀ = span G, so it suffices to show G ⊆ T. Let v ∈ G, witnessed by γ: C¹ on (−1,1), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ M, γ(0) = y₀, and derivative v at 0.
6. γ is differentiable, hence continuous, at 0. Since γ(0) = y₀ ∈ W and W is open, there is τ ∈ (0,1) with γ(t) ∈ W for |t| < τ. Also γ(t) ∈ M for |t| < 1, so γ(t) ∈ W ∩ M for |t| < τ.
7. Let g := Function.invFunOn ψ V and c(t) := g(γ(t)). For |t| < τ, γ(t) ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), hence c(t) ∈ V and ψ(c(t)) = γ(t). Also c(0) = g(ψ(x₀)) = x₀, because ψ is injective on V. By chart_inverse_continuous, g is continuous on W ∩ M. Since γ(t) → y₀ as t → 0 and γ(t) ∈ W ∩ M for |t| < τ, we get c(t) → g(y₀) = x₀ as t → 0.
8. A is injective and ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional, so there is λ > 0 with |Aζ| ≥ λ|ζ| for all ζ ∈ ℝⁿ. Indeed, if n = 0 take λ = 1. Otherwise ζ ↦ |Aζ| is continuous and, by injectivity, positive on the compact nonempty unit sphere, so it has a positive minimum λ there; apply this to ζ/|ζ| for ζ ≠ 0.
9. By step 7 there is τ₁ ∈ (0, τ] with |c(t) − x₀| < δ_{λ/2} for |t| < τ₁. For such t, using ψ(c(t)) = γ(t), step 1 with ε = λ/2, and step 8:
|γ(t) − γ(0)| = |A(c(t) − x₀) + e(c(t))| ≥ λ|c(t) − x₀| − (λ/2)|c(t) − x₀| = (λ/2)|c(t) − x₀|.
Since γ has derivative v at 0, there is τ₂ ∈ (0, τ₁] with |γ(t) − γ(0) − t v| ≤ |t| for |t| < τ₂, so |γ(t) − γ(0)| ≤ (|v| + 1)|t|. Hence ζ(t) := t⁻¹(c(t) − x₀) satisfies |ζ(t)| ≤ C := 2(|v| + 1)/λ for 0 < |t| < τ₂.
10. Let t_j := τ₂/(j + 2) for j ∈ ℕ. Then 0 < t_j < τ₂, t_j → 0 and |ζ(t_j)| ≤ C. By Bolzano–Weierstrass in ℝⁿ, some subsequence s_k := t_{j_k} has ζ(s_k) → ζ for a point ζ ∈ ℝⁿ. Still s_k ≠ 0 and s_k → 0.
11. For every k, |s_k| < τ, so γ(s_k) = ψ(c(s_k)) and
(γ(s_k) − γ(0))/s_k = (A(c(s_k) − x₀) + e(c(s_k)))/s_k = Aζ(s_k) + e(c(s_k))/s_k.
(a) The left side tends to v, because γ has derivative v at 0, s_k → 0 and s_k ≠ 0.
(b) Aζ(s_k) → Aζ, because A is linear on the finite-dimensional ℝⁿ, hence continuous.
(c) e(c(s_k))/s_k → 0. Given ε > 0, c(s_k) → x₀ by step 7, so |c(s_k) − x₀| < δ_ε for large k. Then |e(c(s_k))/s_k| ≤ ε|c(s_k) − x₀|/|s_k| = ε|ζ(s_k)| ≤ εC.
By uniqueness of limits in ℝᴺ, v = Aζ ∈ T. Hence G ⊆ T, and tangentSpace M y₀ = span G ⊆ T.
12. Conclusion. Parts A and B give tangentSpace M (ψ x₀) = T = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ x₀).toLinearMap. Since x₀ ∈ V, and n, N, r, M, V, W, ψ, were arbitrary, the theorem follows.

Formal references (Mathlib): ContDiffOn.differentiableOn, DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt, ContDiffOn.comp, HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt (Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/Comp.lean:374), Submodule.span_le, Submodule.subset_span, Submodule.smul_mem, Function.invFunOn_mem and Function.invFunOn_eq. For step 8: LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith (Analysis/Normed/Module/FiniteDimension.lean:231). For step 10: tendsto_subseq_of_bounded (Topology/MetricSpace/Sequences.lean:38).
proof_key_steps: ψ is C¹ on the open set V, so it is differentiable at x₀ with derivative A = Dψ(x₀) and remainder e(x) = o(|x − x₀|).
range A ⊆ T_{y₀}M: for w ≠ 0, the curve t ↦ ψ(x₀ + c t w) with c = ρ/(2|w|) is C¹ on (−1,1), stays in ψ(V) ⊆ M, and has velocity c·Aw; then divide by c.
T_{y₀}M ⊆ range A, setup: for a generating curve γ, γ(t) ∈ W ∩ M near 0, and the lift c(t) = invFunOn ψ V (γ(t)) tends to x₀ by chart_inverse_continuous.
Injectivity of A gives |Aζ| ≥ λ|ζ|, hence (λ/2)|c(t) − x₀| ≤ |γ(t) − γ(0)| ≤ (|v| + 1)|t|, so ζ(t) = (c(t) − x₀)/t is bounded.
Along a Bolzano–Weierstrass subsequence s_k → 0, the quotient (γ(s_k) − γ(0))/s_k = Aζ(s_k) + e(c(s_k))/s_k tends to both v and Aζ. So v = Aζ ∈ range A, and taking spans finishes the inclusion.

subproblems.title: Orthogonal projection onto the range of an injective linear map depends continuously on the map
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ. Consider the map A ↦ P_{range A} from L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) to L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ), where L(·,·) consists of all linear maps with the operator-norm topology and P_K is the orthogonal projection of ℝᴺ onto the subspace K (Submodule.starProjection). This map is continuous on the set S = {A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) : A injective}, with its relative topology.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ), ContinuousOn (fun A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N ↦ (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).starProjection) {A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N | Function.Injective A}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent-supplied proof of simon_submanifold_tangent_basics (projection onto the range of an injective map, Π(A) = A(A*A)⁻¹A*), written out in full.

Notation. For A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), let A* ∈ L(ℝᴺ, ℝⁿ) be its adjoint, so ⟨A*v, u⟩ = ⟨v, Au⟩. All spaces are finite-dimensional, so L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) is a complete normed ring with unit I. S is the set of injective A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), and P_K is the orthogonal projection onto a subspace K ⊆ ℝᴺ.

Proof.
1. A*A is invertible for A ∈ S. If A*Aζ = 0, then 0 = ⟨A*Aζ, ζ⟩ = ⟨Aζ, Aζ⟩ = |Aζ|², so Aζ = 0 and hence ζ = 0. Thus A*A is an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ. It is therefore bijective, with a linear (and automatically continuous) inverse, so A*A is a unit of L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ).
2. The formula. For A ∈ S, let Π(A) := A(A*A)⁻¹A* and K := range A. Fix v ∈ ℝᴺ and put p := Π(A)v = A((A*A)⁻¹A*v) ∈ K. For each element Au of K (u ∈ ℝⁿ),
⟨v − p, Au⟩ = ⟨A*v − A*A(A*A)⁻¹A*v, u⟩ = ⟨A*v − A*v, u⟩ = 0.
So p ∈ K and v − p ⊥ K. The orthogonal projection P_K v is the unique point of the finite-dimensional, hence closed, subspace K whose difference from v is orthogonal to K. Therefore Π(A)v = P_K v, and Π(A) = P_{range A}. Equivalently, as stated in the parent proof, Π(A) fixes range A, since Π(A)Aζ = A(A*A)⁻¹(A*A)ζ = Aζ, and it kills (range A)^⊥ = ker A*.
3. A globally defined extension. Let inv(B) := B⁻¹ if B ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) is invertible and inv(B) := 0 otherwise (Ring.inverse). Define F(A) := A ∘ inv(A*A) ∘ A* for every A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ). By steps 1–2, F(A) = Π(A) = P_{range A} for every A ∈ S.
4. F is continuous at every A₀ ∈ S.
(a) A ↦ A* is a linear isometry from L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) onto L(ℝᴺ, ℝⁿ), hence continuous.
(b) Composition (B, C) ↦ B ∘ C of continuous linear maps is a bounded bilinear map, hence jointly continuous. So A ↦ A*A is continuous.
(c) In a complete normed ring, inversion is continuous at every unit, by the Neumann series: if B₀ is invertible and |B − B₀| < |B₀⁻¹|⁻¹, then B is invertible, and B⁻¹ → B₀⁻¹ as B → B₀. By step 1, A₀*A₀ is a unit, so inv is continuous at A₀*A₀, and A ↦ inv(A*A) is continuous at A₀.
(d) Combining (a), (b) and (c) with the joint continuity of composition, A ↦ A ∘ inv(A*A) ∘ A* = F(A) is continuous at A₀.
5. Conclusion. Let A₀ ∈ S and let A → A₀ within S. By step 4, F(A) → F(A₀). By step 3, F(A) = P_{range A} and F(A₀) = P_{range A₀}. Hence A ↦ P_{range A} is continuous within S at every A₀ ∈ S, that is, ContinuousOn (fun A ↦ (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).starProjection) S.

Formal references (Mathlib): ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint, a linear isometry equivalence (Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Adjoint.lean:112), and adjoint_inner_left; Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero (Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Projection/Basic.lean:180); ContinuousLinearMap.isUnit_iff_bijective; Ring.mul_inverse_cancel; NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt (Analysis/Normed/Ring/Units.lean:183); Continuous.clm_comp; ContinuousAt.clm_comp; ContinuousWithinAt.congr.
proof_key_steps: For injective A, ⟨A*Aζ, ζ⟩ = |Aζ|² shows A*A is injective, hence invertible in L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ).
Π(A) = A(A*A)⁻¹A* satisfies Π(A)v ∈ range A and v − Π(A)v ⊥ range A, so Π(A) = P_{range A}.
F(A) = A ∘ Ring.inverse(A*A) ∘ A* is continuous at every injective A: the adjoint is an isometry, composition is jointly continuous, and inversion is continuous at units.
F agrees with A ↦ P_{range A} on the injective maps, so the latter is continuous on that set.

subproblems.title: A Simon submanifold is a Borel set (local closedness and Lindelöf)
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, r ∈ ℕ∞ and M ⊆ ℝᴺ with IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝⁿ) r M. That is, 1 ≤ r, and every y ∈ M lies in W for some V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝᴺ and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ with IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ: V and W are open, ψ is C^r on V, ψ is injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(x) is injective for x ∈ V. Then M is a Borel subset of ℝᴺ (MeasurableSet M).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn n) r M → MeasurableSet M
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–6 of the parent-supplied proof of simon_submanifold_tangent_basics (local closedness from relative properness, then Lindelöf), written out in full.

Proof.
1. Local closedness. Let (V, W, ψ) be any local representation of M, so IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ, and let F_W := closure(W ∩ M), a closed set. We claim W ∩ F_W ⊆ M.
Let z ∈ W ∩ F_W. Since ℝᴺ is a metric space, there are z_j ∈ W ∩ M (j ∈ ℕ) with z_j → z. The set Q := {z_j : j ∈ ℕ} ∪ {z} is compact, being a convergent sequence together with its limit, and Q ⊆ W because each z_j ∈ W and z ∈ W. By relative properness, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact.
Since z_j ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), choose x_j ∈ V with ψ(x_j) = z_j; then x_j ∈ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q). By sequential compactness, some subsequence x_{j_k} converges to a point x ∈ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q). ψ is C^r, hence continuous, on the open set V, so it is continuous at x. Therefore ψ(x) = lim_k ψ(x_{j_k}) = lim_k z_{j_k} = z. Hence z ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M ⊆ M, which proves the claim.
2. Consequently W ∩ M = W ∩ F_W. The inclusion '⊆' holds because W ∩ M ⊆ closure(W ∩ M) = F_W, and '⊇' is step 1.
3. Countable subcover (Lindelöf). For every y ∈ M, IsSimonSubmanifold provides a local representation (V_y, W_y, ψ_y) with y ∈ W_y. The sets W_y (y ∈ M) are open and cover M. ℝᴺ is second countable, so there is a countable set C ⊆ M with ∪_{y ∈ C} W_y = ∪_{y ∈ M} W_y ⊇ M.
4. M as a countable union. Every z ∈ M lies in W_y for some y ∈ C. Hence M = ∪_{y ∈ C} (W_y ∩ M) = ∪_{y ∈ C} (W_y ∩ F_{W_y}), using step 2 for each (V_y, W_y, ψ_y).
5. Measurability. Each W_y ∩ F_{W_y} is the intersection of an open set and a closed set, hence Borel. A countable union of Borel sets is Borel, and the measurable structure of ℝᴺ is its Borel σ-algebra. Therefore MeasurableSet M. If M = ∅, then C = ∅ and the statement is trivial.

Formal references (Mathlib): mem_closure_iff_seq_limit (Topology/Sequences.lean:108), Filter.Tendsto.isCompact_insert_range, IsCompact.tendsto_subseq (Topology/Sequences.lean:298), TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable (Topology/Bases.lean:932), IsOpen.measurableSet, IsClosed.measurableSet, MeasurableSet.biUnion.
proof_key_steps: For a local representation (V, W, ψ), relative properness and continuity of ψ on V give W ∩ closure(W ∩ M) ⊆ M. So W ∩ M = W ∩ F_W with F_W = closure(W ∩ M) closed.
The open chart sets W_y (y ∈ M) cover M, and second countability of ℝᴺ gives a countable subfamily with the same union (Lindelöf).
M = ∪_{y ∈ C} (W_y ∩ F_{W_y}) is a countable union of Borel sets of the form open ∩ closed, hence measurable.

subproblems.title: The tangent projection y ↦ P_y is continuous on a Simon submanifold
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, r ∈ ℕ∞ and M ⊆ ℝᴺ with IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝⁿ) r M. That is, 1 ≤ r, and every y ∈ M lies in W for some local representation (V, W, ψ) as in Simon 4.1, i.e. IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ. Then the map y ↦ tangentProjection M y ∈ L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ), the orthogonal projection of ℝᴺ onto tangentSpace M y, is continuous on M. Here M carries the relative topology and L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ) the operator-norm topology.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn n) r M → ContinuousOn (tangentProjection M) M
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent-supplied proof of simon_submanifold_tangent_basics. It uses three sibling theorems: chart_inverse_continuous (parent step 1), tangent_space_eq_range (parent steps 2–4) and range_projection_continuous (parent step 7).

Proof.
1. Fix y₀ ∈ M. By IsSimonSubmanifold, 1 ≤ r, and there are V, W, ψ with y₀ ∈ W and IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ. Put g := Function.invFunOn ψ V and P := tangentProjection M.
2. For y ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), some a ∈ V has ψ(a) = y, so by the definition of invFunOn, g(y) ∈ V and ψ(g(y)) = y.
3. Formula for P on W ∩ M. Let y ∈ W ∩ M and x := g(y) ∈ V. By tangent_space_eq_range, which applies since 1 ≤ r, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) with Dψ(x) = fderiv ℝ ψ x. Since ψ(x) = y, tangentSpace M y = range Dψ(g(y)). P(y) is the orthogonal projection onto tangentSpace M y, so P(y) = P_{range Dψ(g(y))} for every y ∈ W ∩ M.
4. The right side is continuous on W ∩ M.
(a) By chart_inverse_continuous, g is continuous on W ∩ M, and by step 2 it maps W ∩ M into V.
(b) ψ is C^r with r ≥ 1 on the open set V, so x ↦ Dψ(x) is continuous on V. Also Dψ(x) is injective for every x ∈ V (IsSimonLocalRepresentation), so x ↦ Dψ(x) maps V into the set S of injective linear maps.
(c) By range_projection_continuous, A ↦ P_{range A} is continuous on S.
Each map sends its domain into the set on which the next map is continuous. By the composition rule for maps continuous on sets, y ↦ P_{range Dψ(g(y))} is continuous on W ∩ M.
5. By steps 3 and 4, P coincides on W ∩ M with a function that is continuous on W ∩ M, so P is continuous on W ∩ M. In particular, since y₀ ∈ W ∩ M, P is continuous within W ∩ M at y₀.
6. W is open and contains y₀, so W is a neighbourhood of y₀. Therefore the filters of neighbourhoods of y₀ within W ∩ M and within M coincide, and P is continuous within M at y₀.
7. Since y₀ ∈ M was arbitrary, ContinuousOn (tangentProjection M) M.

Formal references (Mathlib): Function.invFunOn_mem, Function.invFunOn_eq, ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen (Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/Defs.lean:916), ContinuousOn.comp, ContinuousOn.congr, continuousWithinAt_inter (Topology/ContinuousOn.lean:259).
proof_key_steps: Fix y₀ ∈ M and a local representation (V, W, ψ) with y₀ ∈ W. Then g = invFunOn ψ V maps W ∩ M into V, and ψ ∘ g = id there.
By tangent_space_eq_range, tangentProjection M y = P_{range Dψ(g(y))} for y ∈ W ∩ M.
Three maps compose to a function continuous on W ∩ M: g (chart_inverse_continuous), x ↦ Dψ(x) (C¹ on open V, with injective values), and A ↦ P_{range A} (range_projection_continuous).
W is a neighbourhood of y₀, so continuity within W ∩ M at y₀ is the same as continuity within M at y₀.
